problems.description: 45 SonarQube convention violations (score 0.52) concentrated on naming: snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, and non-UPPER_CASE constants across cli.ts, config.ts and other added TypeScript files — non-idiomatic for TS/JS, which expects camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE.
Cognitive complexity +19 across only 7 added functions (~2.7 avg) suggests several new functions in the modules are doing too much and could be decomposed.

The 200-line seed index.ts was deleted wholesale rather than built upon. Acceptable for a greenfield SSG session (seed was an unrelated auth API), but the delivered project is entirely new rather than an evolution of the baseline.

strengths: Monolith decomposed into a modular multi-file architecture (+10 files) with clear separation of cli.ts, config.ts, and core modules
Jest/ts-jest test harness added with isolated test roots and clearMocks
SonarQube smells down 4, zero new bugs, zero code duplication introduced
package-lock.json committed, giving reproducible dependency resolution
commit_reviews.summary: A strong greenfield architectural step — the agent correctly discarded the unrelated auth-API seed and scaffolded a modular SSG with tests (better than baseline), but the pervasive non-idiomatic TypeScript naming (45 violations, convention score 0.52) will require a later rename pass; my qualitative read agrees with the mechanical convention score.

problems.description: New templating feature (partials, layouts, template selection) ships with zero tests; no test files in the diff despite a ~160-line behavioral surface
Templates are recompiled via handlebars.compile per page inside the render loop instead of compiling once and caching; cognitive complexity +34 suggests this per-page path is overloaded
loadPartials eagerly reads every .hbs file in the partials tree even when unused, adding I/O on every build
duplications +5.8% and +1 smell: the ENOENT try/catch guard pattern is repeated across fileExists, loadPartials, and templatePath instead of a single helper

Mechanical convention score 0.52 with 45 violations flags PascalCase/UPPER_CASE/snake_case issues in cli.ts and config.ts; the flagged items appear pre-existing (config.ts is untouched) and the new code itself uses consistent camelCase matching the files it edits

strengths: Adds path-traversal protection in templatePath (resolve + prefix check) — a real security concern for template loaders handled correctly
Uses an isolated Handlebars.create() instance and registerPartial, avoiding global registry pollution
Backward compatible: templatesDir is optional with a sensible default, CLI flag added alongside the usage string update, existing build behavior unchanged when no templates dir provided
Follows existing codebase patterns: option-parsing loop, BuildOptions interface extension, fs error handling style consistent with markdownFiles
Correctly moves handlebars and its transitive deps out of devDependencies into runtime dependencies in package-lock.json
commit_reviews.summary: A solid, security-conscious feature addition that fits the SSG architecture and existing patterns, held back by missing tests, per-page template recompilation, and a mechanical convention score that conflicts with my reading (flagged violations appear pre-existing).

problems.description: 45 convention violations in cli.ts and config.ts: functions use snake_case, classes and interfaces are not PascalCase, constants are not UPPER_CASE (measured convention score 0.52).
Cognitive complexity increased by +61 across the new integration code, adding maintainability burden to the watch/live-reload path.
SonarQube delta reports +2 code smells introduced in the touched files.
chokidar and ws are appropriate additions for an SSG integration session (file watching + live-reload server), but they broaden the production dependency surface.

strengths: Dependency selection is idiomatic for the SSG integration session: chokidar for file watching and ws for a live-reload server.

package-lock.json is kept consistent with package.json, including @types/ws correctly declared as a devDependency and transitive deps correctly re-flagged as production (anymatch, braces, fsevents, etc.).
Duplications decreased by 2.1%, indicating the new integration code consolidates rather than copies existing logic.
commit_reviews.summary: Architecturally sound feature addition (watch + websocket integration, properly reflected in the lockfile) but it introduces naming-convention debt across cli.ts/config.ts — agreeing with the measured 0.52 convention score and +61 cognitive complexity.

problems.description: 45 convention violations concentrated in cli.ts and config.ts: functions in snake_case, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE (measured convention score 0.52). Notably, the displayed diff for config.ts is clean camelCase/PascalCase, so the violations must live in the truncated cli.ts and other new files — a discrepancy between what's visible and the measurement, which I treat as ground truth.

config.ts loadTypeScriptModule monkey-patches Module._extensions['.ts'] and clears require.cache — fragile and stateful; a dedicated loader (esbuild-register, ts-node, or a worker-based compile) would be less invasive.

typescript moved from devDependencies to production dependencies to support .ts config loading at runtime; justified architecturally but adds a heavy runtime footprint for what is a build-time concern.
Net cognitive complexity +18 with +581/-377 lines across a 'refactor'; large blast radius, though bugs +0, smells -1, and duplications -0.7% all improve.

strengths: Introduces a clean plugin seam with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onEnd) and a dedicated Plugin/SsgConfig type surface in src/plugin.ts.
Extracts markdown and template concerns into separate plugin modules, reducing coupling in src/index.ts (formerly ~240 lines of mixed concerns).
Config loader supports both .js and .ts config files with default-export fallback and explicit validation error.
SsgEngine class gives an injectable, testable build entry point with resolved options.
commit_reviews.summary: A net-positive, well-structured plugin refactor that is architecturally sound (clean seam, extracted concerns, fewer smells/duplications, zero new bugs) but undercuts itself on conventions — a 0.52 measured convention score with 45 violations in the new files, plus a fragile Module._extensions loader and a heavier runtime dependency, making it 'better' overall while introducing modest technical debt.

problems.description: SonarQube cognitive complexity +42 concentrated in build(), directoryHash() (nested recursion), and readManifest() (defensive validation). The incremental-build branching and manifest parsing are dense and should be decomposed into smaller focused helpers.
The cache manifest (.ssg-cache.json) is written inside the output directory, so it becomes a deployed/served static artifact on every build, leaking build internals into the published site.

Measured convention score 0.52 with 45 violations, but the enumerated violations (Classes/Interfaces PascalCase, Constants UPPER_CASE, snake_case in cli.ts and config.ts) are largely pre-existing — config.ts is untouched by this commit. New code (CachedPage, CacheManifest, BuildStats, CACHE_VERSION) follows TypeScript conventions correctly.

strengths: Versioned cache manifest (CACHE_VERSION) with defensive read validation on version, shape, and field types — no blind trust of cached state.
Correct incremental invalidation via source-content hash + template-directory hash, with output-file existence check as a final guard.
Clean refactor to createEngine()/engine.build() that reuses existing BuildContext and runHook patterns, and exposes lastBuildStats telemetry cleanly.
--incremental/--clean CLI flags gated to the build command with clear usage errors, matching existing arg-parsing style.
Zero new bugs/smells and reduced duplication (-0.6%); cache hits short-circuit the full rebuild pipeline including plugin hooks safely.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-structured incremental-build feature that fits the engine architecture and reuses existing patterns, but the +42 cognitive complexity spike and cache-manifest-in-output-dir placement add moderate maintainability debt; the low 0.52 convention score reflects pre-existing repo violations (e.g. untouched config.ts), not this diff.

compounding_issues: Convention debt (snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, non-UPPER_CASE constants) introduced in Session 1 was never remediated — convention score stuck at 0.523 across all 5 sessions and every reviewer flagged it.
Session 2's per-page Handlebars recompilation and eager partial loading persisted into the plugin era (TemplatePlugin still recompiles per page after the S4 refactor).
Session 3 shipped the dev server as a dense standalone module (+61 cognitive complexity) with untyped `require('chokidar')`/`require('ws')`, forcing Session 4 to relocate it into the plugin system.
Session 4 introduced a fragile `Module._extensions` monkey-patch TypeScript config loader — a new architectural fragility traded for TS-config support.
Session 5 writes the `.ssg-cache.json` manifest inside the output dir, leaking build internals into the served/deployed site.
key_decisions: Session 1 discarded the unrelated auth-API seed entirely and scaffolded a fresh modular buildSite() core — correct given the seed mismatch, but it also fixed the codebase's non-idiomatic naming style.
Session 2 chose Handlebars over EJS, establishing frontmatter template selection plus partials/layouts conventions.
Session 3 built the dev server (chokidar watch + WebSocket live reload) as a standalone module wired into the CLI, before the plugin system existed.

Session 4 extracted the Plugin lifecycle interface (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) and split markdown/template/dev-server into plugins — the pivotal seam that made Session 5's incremental builds clean and testable.
Session 5 implemented hash-based `.ssg-cache.json` caching with source + template-hash invalidation, integrated through the plugin build pipeline rather than bypassing it.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality followed a dip-then-rebound arc. Session 1 started strong with a modular, tested greenfield core (2 tests passing); Session 2 delivered a large templating surface with only light test coverage and per-page compile costs; Session 3 pushed cognitive complexity to +61 with a dense, untyped dev-server module and was the weakest commit. Session 4 was the turning point: the plugin refactor cut complexity and smells, gave the system a clean extension seam, and paid down Session 3's debt by relocating the server into DevServerPlugin. Session 5 then delivered the hardest cross-cutting feature (incremental builds with cache invalidation, stale-output removal, and template-change invalidation) with the strongest test suite in the story. The final state is healthy — all 26 tests across 5 suites pass — though the flat 0.523 convention score persisted as the single unaddressed defect throughout.
story_review.summary: A textbook 5-session arc (greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting) where an early complexity dip and pervasive naming-convention debt were largely redeemed by a pivotal Session 4 plugin refactor and a strong Session 5 that landed a clean, well-tested incremental-build system.
